source_reasoning.finding: I rendered and visually read the held official Federal Register PDF page 1, 14 FR 377. EO 10030 ends after two numbered paragraphs, Truman signature and January 26, 1949 date. EO 10031 and the contents column are neighboring material, not additional EO 10030 commands. Paragraph 1 is a standing administration delegation/direction with an express inapplicability proviso for active Federal service or active emergency duty in DC duly ordered under law. Paragraph 2 is a recurring appointment-recommendation duty, not a one-time appointment or report deadline.

I rendered and visually read all five sections and signature on EO 11485 at 34 FR 15411, PDF page 5, and the correction at 34 FR 15443, PDF page 5. Section 5 expressly supersedes the entire EO 10030, without saving either paragraph, and the present-tense act is dated and filed October 1, 1969 with no deferred commencement. Section 1 supplies a new militia-status administration/command regime; section 3 supplies a new recommendation rule including Attorney General consultation. Those are successor norms, not surviving EO 10030 commands. The October 4 publication corrects the last sentence of section 1 only; it does not alter section 5 or the effective date. This supports terminal supersession, not automatic first-cessation closure for paragraph 1.

I read the held full-act extraction for sections 4, 5, the section 411 inconsistent-provisions clause, and section 12, and visually inspected PDF pages 14-15 / 63 Stat. 591-592. Section 12(g) preserves laws/orders/actions except inconsistency and expressly transfers references/functions to successors, including Department of Defense as successor to the National Military Establishment. Sections 4-5 establish the Department and the Secretary direction/delegation structure. No inconsistency terminating these two EO 10030 commands appears in the examined provisions. The first one-page 63 Stat. 578 retrieval cannot supply section 12(g); the distinct 15-page retrieval does.

I read the actual held official HTML bytes of 32 USC 110 historical notes and Title 32 frontmatter. The revision notes map former 32 USC 17 / 1916 section 118 to section 110. The quoted 1956 Act section 49 states restatement without substantive change, reference conversion and preserved acts; section 50 retains preexisting suspended/temporarily superseded status, and section 53 is subject to section 49. These are continuity provisions, not a new termination or revival of EO 10030. The frontmatter is a later official compilation current through October 15, 2026; I use its quoted historical text only, not as proof of current law at the October 14 cutoff. I did not inspect an original 1956 Statutes at Large page.

I visually read the actual 71 Stat. 596 page. The relevant Act is Public Law 85-270, September 2, 1957, not the erroneous initial PL85-251 request label. It permits brigadier or major general rank and replaces an adjutant-detail reference to brigadier-general commanding with commanding general of. It does not name or terminate EO 10030, abolish its recurring recommendation duty, or demonstrate a first ending of paragraph 2. The corrected request preserves the same raw PDF hash.

I visually read EO 11403 in full at 33 FR 5501, PDF page 11. Section 3(a) authorizes/directs the Secretary to call units or members into active military service as appropriate, until relieved; section 3(b) separately delegates militia powers for members not called into active service. The order neither names EO 10030 nor itself identifies actual called units and release dates. Under the owner unnamed-instrument ruling it is a disclosed earlier candidate, not an unexpressed permanent repeal. The EO 10030 proviso still requires factual and legal application review.

I rendered and visually read the 2007 hearing PDF pages 25-29 / printed pages 21-25, including Blum statement scope and the 1,854 DC National Guard entry for April 5-16, 1968. The table is expressly limited to Insurrection Act federalizations since WWII, not all federal callups or emergency duty. I also independently rendered and read CMH PDF pages 307-308 and 316-317 / printed pages 287-288 and 296-297. The history reports federalization at 1700 on April 5, delayed assembly, 40 percent present then 97 percent / 1,854 by April 15, and release from federal service at midnight following the Tuesday April 16 sequence. Those are retrospective official factual evidence; I did not read the cited original DA 858687 message, DCNG AAR, or TFW AAR. I do not convert these findings into a certified earliest clause end or a complete unit-by-unit resumption history.

source_reasoning.topic: earlier unit episodes and emergency duty
source_reasoning.finding: The held archived official DCNG history reports the 715th Truck Company mobilization in 1951 and 113th Wing activation in 1961 and 1968, without complete exact callup/release dates or order texts. I read that content and verified the archived raw HTML hash. I visually read CMH printed pages 241-242 and 250-251 / PDF pages 261-262 and 270-271: the discussion distinguishes militia special-police status, the 1963 precedent, and planned possible federalization in 1967. It does not justify treating every police detail as duly ordered active emergency duty. Source-v8 records two no_route outcomes for actual unit and operational records, with zero acquisition attempts; this is a route limitation, not exhaustive archival search. Source-v7 is absent in this checkout.

source_reasoning.topic: bounded later search and present status
source_reasoning.finding: I read the frozen base EVIDENCE and its qualified OFR observations: incoming/outgoing catalog relations share editorial provenance and the 1989 layer is only an ended-by bound. I independently replayed the provided local regexes across 6,652 held text files and obtained the same seven matching files; checked the 23,858-row edge file hash and five target rows; excluded page-number and neighboring-order matches; and read EO 14339 held text in full, finding no revival of EO 10030. Supplemental independent indexed web queries produced NARA/OFR corroboration of supersession and no identified revival. These are bounded searches with sparse-corpus/OCR/index limitations. They support the NO status hypothesis and retained terminal end, not completeness of historical episodes. Status adoption remains separate.

All 39 manifest raw/extracted/receipt hash checks matched, as did every quoted candidate text span and text-file hash. Official FR PDFs supply the target and acting text here, so these claims are not built solely on APP/OFR editorial transcriptions. The archived DCNG and CMH representations remain archived official-origin material; the hearing and CMH are retrospective factual accounts, not the underlying operational instruments. HTML historical notes remain compilations. No source custody verification, original page inspection, or AI review here changes canonical authentication, status, owner acceptance, human certification, or readiness credit.
